bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: The company's focus on sustainable infrastructure and logistics could provide a competitive advantage in the long term
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Balance sheet as of 30th June 2026: "Cash and Bank balance of Rs 9,863 Crore and Gross Debt of Rs 7,094 Crore", after a "Successfully completed QIP of Rs 7,503 crore backed by marquee global and domestic investors".
- Leverage trend shown FY21 to FY26: Net debt/Equity 1.17x, 0.96x, 0.54x, 0.01x, 0.14x, 0.27x; Net debt/Operating EBITDA 4.42x, 3.00x, 1.37x, 0.03x, 0.65x, 1.19x.
- Ratings: Fitch BBB-/Stable, S&P Global BBB-/Stable, Moody's Baa3/Stable (newly secured in the quarter) and domestic CARE AA+/Stable — "well positioned to pursue value-accretive organic and inorganic growth".
- Stated growth lever: "Leveraging Balance Sheet for inorganic growth opportunities in port and port-related infrastructure", alongside "Privatisation Bids - Balancing sustained growth".
- Returns have compressed as capital is deployed: RoCE (on average capital employed) shown as 8.9% FY21, 11.0% FY22, 18.8% FY23, 20.9% FY24, 16.9% FY25, 14.9% FY26 and 13.4% at Jun-26 (TTM, versus 17.2% at Jun-25).
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body: Paradip East Quay Coal Terminal Private Limited is a subsidiary of JSW Infrastructure Ltd, operating in the coal terminal segment
business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
- "JSW Infrastructure is the second largest private port operator in India with 186 mtpa capacity", with "Strategically located assets with well equipped Ports and Terminals with Multi-Modal Evacuation Channels".
- Moat framing: "Locational advantage enhances sticky cargo profile that leads to lower transportation costs" and "Diversified presence ensures good connectivity to industrial hinterlands and mineral rich belts", across both the West and East coasts of India.
- Anchor-customer model: JSW Steel is named the "Strong Anchor Customer"; in Q1 FY27 the customer mix was JSW Group 52% / Third Party 48% (Q1 FY26: JSW Group 48% / Third Party 52%).
- Sector framing: "Well placed to reap the benefits of the growing Indian economy, massive infra build, strong cargo growth potential and limited competition in the sector", plus "benefits of Government's Privatization drive".
- International footprint beyond the 186 mtpa: O&M contracts at two dry bulk terminals in the UAE — Fujairah (24 mtpa) and Dibba (17 mtpa) — which the deck explicitly excludes from operational capacity.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Group context — not the listed entity] The deck opens with a JSW Group page: conglomerate turnover of US$25 Bn (as of FY26), Steel 33.4 MTPA growing to 50.3 mtpa by FY30 and 63.5 mtpa by FY32, Energy 14.54 GW targeting 30GW plus 40GWh storage by FY30, Cement 24.1 MTPA growing to 46 MTPA, Paints 535,000+ KLPA targeting 800,000 KLPA by FY30, plus EV, Sports and Ventures. Infrastructure's own market cap is given as ~US$8 Bn (as of July 30, 2026).
- [Acquisition — Paints, group level] "Completed transformative acquisition of Akzo Nobel India (now known as JSW Dulux), with a shareholding of 61.2%" — a group-level item, not JSW Infrastructure.
- [Concessions won] Concession signed/awarded but not yet operational: Keni 30.0, Murbe 33.0, Jatadhar 30.0, Ash Shiwaymiyyah Port (Oman) 27.0, Kolkata Outer Container Terminal 13.0, JNPA Liquid Terminal 4.5, V.O.C Tuticorin Bulk 7.0 and Kolkata Container Terminal 6.3 (Ports - 120 mtpa, Terminals - 26.3 mtpa).
- [Approvals] "Secured Environmental Clearance and approval for rail connectivity to the DFC for Murbe Port in Maharashtra, marking a key development milestone"; for Jatadhar, a "Novation agreement for port concession executed with anchor customer post Odisha Government approval".
- [Regulation] Appendix explains the Indian Railways GPWIS and LSFTO licence regimes (launch years 2018 and 2020; freight rebates of 10% for 15 years capped at capital recovery, and 12% for 20 years) which underpin the rake-fleet plan; the deck's column-to-scheme mapping is not preserved in extraction, so which rebate belongs to which scheme is not asserted.

deepdive.thesis: JSW Infrastructure Ltd, a leading port infrastructure company, has received a credit rating of CARE AA with a stable outlook for its subsidiary Paradip East Quay Coal Terminal Private Limited, indicating a strong financial position and stable cash flows. The company's focus on sustainable infrastructure and logistics is expected to drive growth. With a strong parent company and a well-performing subsidiary, JSW Infrastructure Ltd is well-positioned for future expansion.

open.item: Jatadhar Port (Odisha) construction targeted for completion by March 2027; environmental clearance obtained for 52 MTPA (initial 30 MTPA), 80% of pile foundation works and 7 million CBM of dredging completed during FY2026.

Jatadhar Port construction is progressing as planned and is targeted for completion by March 2027; environmental clearance obtained for capacity of up to 52 MTPA (initial 30 MTPA), with 80% of pile foundation works and 7 million CBM of dredging completed during FY2026.
A 302-kilometre iron ore slurry pipeline is expected to be completed by March 2027, shifting iron ore logistics from road/rail to pipeline for the anchor customer.
Aims to more than double its cargo handling capacity to approximately 400 MTPA by FY2030 or earlier.
Aims to more than double cargo handling capacity to approximately 400 MTPA by FY2030 or earlier.
Planned investment of Rs 9,000 crore in the logistics segment over FY2025-2030 to build a robust, integrated pan-India logistics network, building on the Navkar acquisition.
Strategy to expand total ports and terminals capacity to approximately 400 MTPA by 2030, more than doubling current capacity.
FY2025-30 capex allocation earmarked for the Ports business of Rs 30,000 crore.
Planned segment capex of Rs 9,000 crore for the logistics business and Rs 30,000 crore for the ports business over FY2025-30.
Kolkata Container Terminal (0.45 million TEUs / 6.3 MTPA) under DBFOT concession signed September 2025; detailed engineering in progress with interim operations expected to commence soon.
Approximately 302 km underground slurry pipeline connecting Nuagaon mines to Jagatsinghpur (near Jatadhar Port); 235 km of pipeline lowering completed during FY2026.

JSW Kolkata Container Terminal Private Limited executed a DBFOT concession agreement (September 2025) for Berths 7 and 8 at Netaji Subhas Dock, Kolkata, with capacity of 0.45 million TEUs (6.3 MTPA); detailed engineering in progress.
Developing a 27 MTPA greenfield bulk port at Dhofar, Oman through a 51% stake in the Port SPV (Ash Shiwaymiyyah Port Company SAOC), with an estimated investment of USD 419 million.

Kudathini (Ballari, Karnataka) brownfield rail siding, spanning over 86 acres, acquired for approximately Rs 65 crore; being developed into a Multi-Modal Logistics Park (ICD + Rail Freight Terminal) at a total estimated project cost of Rs 380 crore, deployed over the next few years; interim operations already commenced.
Brownfield expansion projects progressing with capacity additions of 21 MTPA at Dharamtar and 15 MTPA at Jaigarh Ports, aligned with a 5 MTPA steel capacity expansion at Dolvi.
Proposed Expansion of Dharamtar Jetty Facility (Phase-III) in village Dolvi, District Raigad, Maharashtra is under EIA process initiated December 2025.
Jaigarh Port capacity expansion from 67.7 MTPA to 80 MTPA received Environmental Clearance in November 2025.
Slurry pipeline (~302 km underground) from Nuagaon mines to Jagatsinghpur, Odisha, connecting to Jatadhar Port vicinity; 235 km of pipeline lowering completed during FY2026.

Ash Shiwaymiyyah Port, Oman greenfield port with initial proposed capacity of 27 MTPA to handle industrial minerals, following the November 2025 Share Subscription and Purchase Agreement; port handling effective from Commercial Operation Date (COD).
Keni Port (30 MTPA) public hearing completed, awaiting Environmental Clearance.

drhp.business: JSW Infrastructure develops and operates ports and terminals under long-term (typically 30-50 year) concessions, offering cargo handling, storage, logistics and value-added services across dry bulk, break bulk, liquid bulk, gases and containers on India's west and east coasts. Founded in 2004 to serve JSW Steel and other group companies, it expanded from 2019 to serve third-party customers (48% of FY2026 cargo) and is now building an integrated port-led logistics platform spanning ICDs/CFS, rail rakes and Gati Shakti Multi-Modal Cargo Terminals through the Navkar Corporation acquisition and …
drhp.end_markets: India - west coast (Maharashtra, Goa, Karnataka)|India - east coast (Odisha, West Bengal, Tamil Nadu)|Industrial regions - Andhra Pradesh, Telangana|Mineral-rich hinterland - Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, Odisha|UAE (Fujairah, Dibba)|Oman (planned, via SPV collaboration)
drhp.expansion: Installed cargo handling capacity grew to 183 MTPA in FY2026 (from 177 MTPA in FY2025 and 170 MTPA in FY2024), and the Company targets more than doubling this to approximately 400 MTPA by FY2030 or earlier through greenfield developments, brownfield expansions, port connectivity projects and diversification into liquid, gas and container cargo. Brownfield expansion is progressing at Dharamtar (+21 MTPA) and Jaigarh (+15 MTPA), aligned with a 5 MTPA steel capacity expansion at Dolvi. risks.note: IMF projects global growth slowing to 3.1% in CY2026 and 3.2% in CY2027 as geopolitical tensions, particularly the Middle East conflict, weigh on economic activity; the conflict has driven disruptions to commodity markets, tighter financial conditions and elevated energy prices, which can affect global trade flows and cargo volumes relevant to the Company's port business.

Higher US tariffs could weigh on India's exports and manufacturing activity in subsequent quarters; since export/import cargo movement is a direct driver of the Company's volumes, sustained tariff or trade-policy shocks are a demand risk.
risks.risk: US tariff escalation and trade-policy uncertainty

risks.note: Material related-party transactions during the year were between wholly-owned subsidiaries JSW Jaigarh Port Limited and JSW Dharamtar Port Private Limited with JSW Steel Limited, and JSW Port Logistics Private Limited with JSW Shipping & Logistics Private Limited, indicating continued dependence on JSW Group cargo and captive/group-company relationships even as third-party cargo share grows.
risks.risk: Anchor-customer / related-party concentration with the JSW Group

risks.note: The Company's Enterprise Risk Management Framework explicitly acknowledges that compliance-related, operational and strategic risks can disrupt operations and affect the achievement of its objectives, requiring continuous risk identification, assessment and mitigation across a large multi-site port and logistics network.
risks.risk: Compliance, operational and strategic risk under the Company's own ERM framework

risks.note: RBI projects that persistently elevated energy prices due to the West Asia conflict, along with possible El Nino conditions, could pose upside risks to inflation — a cost pressure relevant to the fuel- and power-intensive nature of port and cargo-handling operations.
risks.risk: Energy price and input-cost volatility linked to the West Asia conflict

risks.note: As a cargo handling and maritime logistics operator, the Company targets a 'Zero Harm' environment and has invested in a Safety Experience Centre, AI-enabled monitoring and Permit-to-Work systems, indicating that workplace/operational safety across ports, terminals and last-mile logistics remains a material risk area requiring continuous management attention.
risks.risk: Health, safety and environment risk inherent to cargo-handling operations
